name: OWEB Focused Investment Partnership (FIP) Initiatives
summary: Six-year funding for high-performing partnerships delivering restoration, acquisition, technical assistance, engagement and monitoring work plans in Oregon, around board-set priorities such as aquatic habitat, dry forest, estuaries, oak and prairie, closed-lakes wetlands and sage-steppe. Core partners such as tribes, watershed councils and nonprofits apply.

amount.note: Cap per partnership is $5 million per biennium and up to $15 million over the 6-year Initiative

steps: Board Committee interview of Core Partners

eligibility.rule: Have a high-performing partnership with successful collaborative implementation history and documented governance
Have a current Strategic Action Plan addressing a FIP ecological priority and including all required elements
Have a detailed Initiative Work Plan using the FIP Work Plan Template
Core Partner that is a Tribe, watershed council, SWCD, nonprofit, school, college or non-state public body
Have Work Plan projects aligned with the Strategic Action Plan's Strategies and Conservation Actions

documents: Letter of participation signed by each Core Partner
Color maps of the initiative area
Initiative budget for each biennium, on the budget form

window.quote: Offered: FIP initiative applications are solicited once each biennium.

effort.quote: Partnerships interested in applying for a FIP initiative must schedule a 1-hour, virtual pre-application consultation with OWEB to be eligible to apply.
Opened: February 18, 2026 - Closed: 5 pm (Pacific Time), July 13, 2026
An Expert Review Team evaluates, ranks, and provides a funding recommendation based on the information provided and according to criteria described in OAR 695-047-0060 and OAR 695-005-0045.
Board Committee interviews Core Partners proposing an Initiative and makes a funding recommendation to the Board

eligibility.quote: Are high performing, as demonstrated through a shared history of successful, collaborative project implementation and an established, documented Partnership governance (Archived*)
Have a current Strategic Action Plan that includes all elements described in OWEB's Strategic Action Plan Guidance (Archived*) and addresses a FIP ecological priority
Have a detailed Initiative Work Plan using the FIP Work Plan Template.

Eligible Applicants for a FIP Initiative award include any Core Partner that is a Tribe, watershed council, soil and water conservation district, not-for-profit corporation, school, Oregon institution of higher education, independent not-for-profit institution of higher education, or political subdivision of this state that is not a state agency.

Eligible Work Plan Projects include Engagement, Technical Assistance, Restoration, Monitoring, Land Acquisition, and Water Acquisition projects that align with the Strategies and Conservation Actions described in a Partnership's Strategic Action Plan.
OWEB may enter into agreements only with legally established entities.

co_finance.quote: engagement, technical assistance, and monitoring grants requiring 5% match and restoration and acquisition grants requiring 25% match.

after_award.quote: Refer to the front page and Exhibit B of your grant agreement for report deadlines and format of required progress reports.

documents.quote: Proposed Initiative Work Plans must be submitted with the Initiative Application.
A letter of participation on the applicant’s letterhead that includes the authorized signature(s) from each Core Partner
Color map(s) that illustrate the geographical boundary and major features of the proposed initiative.
The Initiative Budget for each biennium using the FIP Initiative Budget Form Upload.
